author: aleda145
text: Great stack! I'm doing a similar approach for my latest project (kavla.dev) but using fly.io and their suspend feature. Scaling to zero with database persistence using litestream has cut my bill down to $0.1 per month for my backend+database. Granted I still don't have that many users, and they get 200ms of extra latency if the backend needs to wake up. But it's nice to never have to worry about accidental costs!

threadTitle: I run multiple $10K MRR companies on a $20/month tech stack
author: AlexSalikov
text: Similar approach here. I run a side project on Next.js + Vercel (free tier) + Neon Postgres (free tier). Total hosting cost: $0/month. The one place I'd push back on SQLite: if your app has any write concurrency from external processes (cron jobs, webhooks), WAL mode helps but you still hit lock contention. I have data collection scripts running every 30 minutes that write to the same DB the web app reads from. Postgres handled that cleanly from day one. Neon's free tier is 512MB with connection pooling — more than enough for a side project with real data.

threadTitle: I run multiple $10K MRR companies on a $20/month tech stack
author: dehrmann
text: A job in tech will get you $10k MRR. At least from this blog post, I wouldn't take his advice on MRR. He's optimizing in the wrong places; he'd be better off spending $100 per month on hosting and focusing on MRR than focusing on bringing hosting costs down to 0.2% of revenue. There's a middle ground without K8S where you use your cloud's autoscaling app hosting and a small, replicated DB. He strawmaned the enterprise approach, and he's trading off a lot of toil for uptime.
